solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criminal pair from Yorkshire heartlessly conned a blind invalid

indicators.note: invalid read as in-VAL-id, not valid or sound, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
heartlessly strips out the middle of Yorkshire, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shady duo from Yorkshire cruelly swindles a sightless sick person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yorkshire heartlessly' gives YE, which joins CONNED, A and BLIND as the letters that 'invalid' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous 1930s American outlaw couple who robbed banks together are the archetypal criminal duo.

clue.text: Leading lady acting in alternative theatre performance

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces sit inside the word for alternative

parts.note: an option is an alternative, one choice among others
the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, abbreviated ER, is the nation's leading lady
A is a standard abbreviation for acting, as in an acting officer

explanation.surface: A star actress performs in an alternative, fringe theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts 'theatre' with 'alternative'; it belongs with 'performance', meaning what surgeons do in an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery is carried out in an operating theatre, so a surgical procedure is literally a performance in a theatre.

clue.text: Explosive ingredient is undisturbed, oddly ignored

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions of undisturbed are skipped and the even ones kept

explanation.surface: Some component of a bomb sits there calmly, strangely left alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a key component of gunpowder.

clue.text: Taking care of monies, could be expert ultimately?

definitions.text: Taking care of monies, could be expert ultimately?

indicators.note: could be says these letters might form something else when rearranged

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the abbreviation for care of on an address

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of expert

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after money might turn out to be a specialist in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' is a link word; 'could be' rearranges CO and MONIES, and 'ultimately' adds the last letter of 'expert'.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in money and the management of resources, someone whose expertise covers finances, describes this profession.

clue.text: Not all listen as alarm's sounded from hooter

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An alarm blares, and not everyone pays attention to its sound from the horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooter is slang for the nose, so a sound made through the nose is a nasal one.

clue.text: Dog with a part cut off? That's docked

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to tail fruit or vegetables is to snip off their ends, so tailed means with a part cut off

explanation.surface: A dog missing part of itself, its tail perhaps, is said to be docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Docked can mean cut short or reduced, as in docked wages, which is a synonym of shortened.

clue.text: One poet or another exchanges krona for yen

indicators.note: exchanges ... for signals that one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: another poet here is John Keats
K is the abbreviation for the Swedish krona
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A currency-trading poet swaps Swedish money for Japanese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' and 'for' are link words; the K of KEATS becomes Y.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Put out flame once metal has constant temperature

parts.note: an old flame is a former lover, an ex
tin is a metal
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Extinguish a fire that once had metal and steady heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire that has been put out, no longer burning, is described this way, as with an inactive volcano.

clue.text: More than one plain maiden pops round

indicators.note: round means the word for pops surrounds the maiden letter

parts.note: pops and papas are both words for fathers
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A plain-looking young woman calls in on her father.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'plain' an adjective; it is a noun, and the answer is the plural of pampa, a South American grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The grassy lowland plains of South America, especially Argentina, are known by this plural name.

clue.text: King cutting a doctor's head off

indicators.note: cutting means the king letter slices into the word for doctor

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor; the 's is a link
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch beheading a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' looks like part of the beheading story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To head off trouble is to prevent it, which is to ward it off.

clue.text: Old baron needs flunkey to be attentive

parts.note: a flunkey is a liveried servant

explanation.surface: An aged nobleman requires a footman to be watchful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attentive notices everything, which is to be watchful and alert.

clue.text: In lead, fifty-one to nil? It has no effect

indicators.note: In places the fifty-one letters inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ace is a one in cards
nil is zero, written O

explanation.surface: Leading fifty-one to nil, yet it makes no difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word placing O after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given in trials contains no active drug, so it should have no medical effect.

clue.text: Hero capturing capital — capital of Soviet Union

indicators.note: capturing means the word for hero holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a lion is a celebrated person, a hero
A1, written AI, means first-rate or capital

indicators.note: capital of means the first letter of Soviet

explanation.surface: A hero seizes a city, the capital of the Soviet Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is used twice: first as the adjective excellent, then for an initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A union can be an alliance or connection, a close relationship, often a secret romantic affair.

clue.text: Rock or jazz music

definitions.meaning: to rock is to sway back and forth
a style of big-band jazz of the 1930s and 1940s

explanation.surface: Choosing between rock and jazz music.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaying to and fro is to rock, and the big-band jazz style of the 1930s has this name.

clue.text: Relative lost rag about Earl's mocking comment

indicators.note: about means the shuffled rag goes around the earl letter
lost suggests letters that have gone astray and are jumbled

parts.note: a taunt is a jeering remark

explanation.surface: A relative loses a newspaper over an aristocrat's sneering remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges RAG to GRA, which goes around E; the 's is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's aunt is a family member two generations above you.

clue.text: Generous, popular fellow will be after flat shortly

indicators.note: will be after places the fellow word behind the flat one

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: shortly cuts the last letter off the word for flat

parts.note: dull means flat or lifeless
a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A kind, well-liked man is soon going to come after an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home; it means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous, lenient person tends to give in to others' wishes freely.

clue.text: Criminal suspect posed entertaining challenge, on reflection

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so one piece sits inside the other
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters of posed are scrambled
on reflection means the word for challenge is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: a dare is a challenge

explanation.surface: A shady suspect sets a fun challenge, after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges POSED to DESPO, which holds ERAD, DARE read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless outlaw of the Wild West is a classic example of a criminal.

clue.text: Priest gets minister put away for murder

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible who trained Samuel
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A priest has a minister locked up for murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' suggests prison but means ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To do away with someone, to kill them, is a common euphemism for murder.

clue.text: Ravel score not containing contralto pieces

indicators.note: containing means the shuffled letters hold the contralto letter
to ravel is to tangle, so the letters of score not get mixed

explanation.surface: A score by Ravel without any contralto parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel the composer is a false lead: the word means tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Works for a soloist with orchestra are musical pieces of a particular kind.

clue.text: Speaker's three-dimensional compartment

indicators.note: Speaker's means according to the way someone talks, as the word is pronounced

parts.note: cubical means shaped like a cube, three-dimensional

explanation.surface: The Speaker of the House has a three-dimensional office.
explanation.definitionFit: A small partitioned space such as an office booth or changing room is a compartment.

clue.text: Spin doctor's a kind of drip with energy

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor; the 's is a link
an IV is an intravenous drip
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor is a sort of feeble drip full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin doctor' is a phrase in the surface; 'Spin' alone is the definition, as in going for a spin in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A short ride for pleasure in a car, going for a spin, is an outing of this kind.

clue.text: Still supports English league team

indicators.note: supports in a down clue means this piece sits below the others

parts.note: still and even both intensify, as in still better or even better

explanation.surface: Someone still backs an English league side.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players, so the number names a team.

clue.text: But arrest's set back, securing right hiding place for the present?

indicators.note: securing means holding the right letter inside
set back means the words are written in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written
to nab is to arrest; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A detention is postponed, but the cell holds the gift for now.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British party or fete game, a lucky dip of presents buried in bran. 'set back' turns BUT NAB into BANTUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Presents are concealed in bran inside the tub until a lucky child digs them out, so it hides gifts.

clue.text: Stomach is tender in casualty?

indicators.note: in means the offer word goes inside the casualty letters

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital casualty department
to tender is to offer, to bid

explanation.surface: A sore belly in the emergency ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like a body part; here it is the verb tolerate. A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: What? Old boy turned up with Australian for tea?

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: An old Aussie fellow turns up asking 'What?' about tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A black China tea, once the most popular kind in England, carries this name.

clue.text: Marshal in Spain went for braid

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A military marshal in Spain went for a gold-braided uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like a rank but is a verb meaning arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To braid is to plait strands together, twisting them around one another.

clue.text: Bad time to withdraw soldiers

indicators.note: to withdraw means to go back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: poor means bad or of low quality

explanation.surface: A poor moment for the soldiers to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of cavalry or a body of soldiers is called by this name.

clue.text: Dog is companion I ditch when going round a couple of universities

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: going, with round, says the ditch word travels around the university letters, here the second one
round says the ditch word wraps a university letter inside it, here the first one

parts.note: a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a hidden boundary in landscaped grounds
U is the abbreviation for university, so two of them give UU
U is the abbreviation for university, so two of them give UU

explanation.surface: A dog is my pal; I abandon it while touring two universities.
explanation.walkthrough: Each U goes inside HAHA after an H. A ha-ha is a ditch-and-wall boundary in English country-house gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny breed of dog originating in Mexico, one of the smallest in the world.

clue.text: Nothing gets one out of angry harangue

parts.note: nothing is zero, written O

indicators.note: out of says the letter for one leaves the word for angry

parts.note: irate means angry
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Achieving nothing makes someone furious enough to rant.
explanation.definitionFit: To harangue is to deliver a long pompous speech, to declaim in that manner.

clue.text: Lear etc cryptically represented problem relating to parents

parts.note: the letters of Lear etc are a jumbled form of the Greek heroine's name, and the clue's next words say that name has been made intricate, or mixed up

explanation.surface: King Lear and similar plays depict trouble between parents and children.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, its first word as fodder and its second as an anagram signal, and you get LEAR ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology this is a daughter's unconscious attachment to her father and rivalry with her mother, a hang-up concerning parents.
